dedupe_keys.name: hype hydrological predictions for the environment semi distributed hydrological and water quality model

description: HYPE is an open source, dynamic and semi-distributed hydrological model that integrates fluxes of water, nutrients and other substances; SMHI produced it and develops and maintains it. Its model description covers processes above the ground, land routines, rivers and lakes, nitrogen and phosphorus in land and in rivers and lakes, water management, deep processes, organic carbon and tracers. Coverage is any catchment that can be set up in its file format. The source code is a free download from SourceForge, with a wiki documenting the model, the file reference, tutorials and the code (Doxygen pages). Caveats: a set-up needs catchment files, forcing and observations for calibration, described in the file reference. Simulation uses: river flows and reservoir and abstraction effects for flood and drought hazard, climate adaptation and water resource planning. Related records: wflow (model-wflow) and the NOAA National Water Model (model-noaa-national-water-model).
